subject: Dedicated capacity — pricing & sizing follow-up (GPU type, reserved size, throughput)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — pricing & sizing follow-up (GPU type, reserved size, throughput)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time this morning — great discussion and really like the way FinLytics is using embeddings + reranking in production. Per our call, I wanted to capture the details we discussed and the open items for pricing a Dedicated capacity offer:

Summary from call:
- Current workload: batch + low-latency API for search & summarization.
- Expected token volume: ~250M tokens/day (batch peak) and ~5M tokens/day (API/live), total ~255M tokens/day (~7.65B tokens/month).
- Latency SLO for live API: p95 < 250ms for prompt+generation (avg gen length ~120 tokens).
- Peak concurrent queries: ~120 concurrent sessions; typical burst-to-burst 200 sessions.
- Successful models: LlamaX-13B quantized variant for cost sensitivity; interested in a path to H100-backed variants for lower latency.

Key pricing/qualification questions (confirm please):
1) Target budget range for Dedicated capacity (monthly committed spend)? You mentioned a ballpark but didn’t lock — can you confirm a range (e.g., $60k–$150k/mo)?
2) GPU preference: do you require H100s for p95 latency, or is an A100/80GB cluster acceptable if the software-level latency meets your SLO via batching and caching?
3) Desired reserved capacity size: do you want a baseline (e.g., 8 GPUs) with burst to 16 GPUs, or do you prefer a larger baseline?
4) Unit economics target: you mentioned target $/1M tokens — is $15–$25/1M tokens an acceptable target?

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm budget range and strong preference for GPU type (A100 vs H100).
- I’ll run a short sizing + throughput calc with Marcus and get back with 2 recommended configs (cost-optimized and latency-optimized) plus target $/1M tokens and a sample monthly commit quote.
- If those look good, we’ll send a formal proposal and schedule a technical sizing session with your infra team.

I attached the MAP doc we referenced. I’ll loop Marcus and Marissa internally to pull numbers.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@finlytics.com>

Date: 2027-04-11T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — pricing & sizing follow-up (GPU type, reserved size, throughput)

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the recap, that looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Volume: the 255M tokens/day is peak on batch processing days; average daily across month will be closer to ~150M/day. For planning, please size for the peak but show steady-state and peak scenarios.
- Budget: we’re targeting $80k–$120k/month for the Dedicated commit. Upper end possible if latency savings justify it.
- GPU: our preference is H100 if it meaningfully reduces latency and improves tokens/sec, but we’re open to an A100 baseline + H100 for bursts if that’s a cost win.
- Target unit economics: ideally <= $20/1M tokens; we can stretch to $25/1M if latency improves.

Also, Tom (CTO) will want a throughput estimate in tokens/sec per GPU for both LlamaX-13B (q4_0 and q8_0) and the H100-optimized kernel we discussed.

Happy to hop on a short call if you need more details.

—Sarah
Sarah Chen
Head of ML Engineering, FinLytics
sarah.chen@finlytics.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — pricing & sizing follow-up (GPU type, reserved size, throughput)

Marissa / Marcus —

Looping you both in. FinLytics confirmed budget target $80k–$120k/mo and target <= $20/1M tokens (stretch to $25). They prefer H100 if latency gains are material but are open to hybrid A100 baseline + H100 burst.

Ask: can you sketch two recommended Dedicated configs with ballpark pricing (monthly commit) and an estimated $/1M tokens: 1) Cost-optimized (A100 baseline) 2) Latency-optimized (H100 baseline). Also include throughput estimates (tokens/sec per GPU) for LlamaX-13B q4_0 and H100-optimized kernel.

Marcus — please include assumptions on batching, KV cache hit rate (assume 30% cross-request prefix cache hit), and any recommended autoscale/burst policy.

Sarah: I’ll share numbers as soon as Marcus and Marissa confirm.

Thanks,
—Dylan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@finlytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — pricing & sizing follow-up (GPU type, reserved size, throughput)

Dylan / Marcus / Sarah —

Following up with preliminary sizing & pricing based on the inputs. High-level assumptions:
- Model: LlamaX-13B (two quant configs): q4_0 (lowest mem) and q8_0 (better quality). Average generation length 120 tokens.
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV): 30% assumed for steady state; burst reduces hit rate to 15%.
- Target p95 latency <250ms for live API.

Recommended configs (baseline + burst):
1) Cost-optimized (A100 baseline)
- Baseline: 8x A100-80GB reserved GPUs
- Burst: +8 GPUs (up to 16) allowed for 25% of bursts
- Estimated tokens/sec per GPU (LlamaX-13B q4_0): 800–1,100 tokens/sec (H100 would be ~1.6x)
- Estimated monthly throughput (baseline): ~8 GPUs * 1,000 tps * 86,400s/day * 30 days * (1 - 0.30 cache) ≈ 1.45B tokens/month (steady-state)
- Estimated unit cost delivered: ~$18–$22 / 1M tokens (depending on commit term and effective burst usage)
- Ballpark monthly commit price: $75k–$95k/mo

2) Latency-optimized (H100 baseline)
- Baseline: 6x H100 reserved GPUs
- Burst: +6 GPUs (up to 12) for peaks
- Estimated tokens/sec per GPU (H100 optimized kernel, LlamaX-13B q8_0): 1,600–2,000 tokens/sec
- Estimated monthly throughput (baseline): ~6 GPUs * 1,800 tps * 86,400s/day * 30 days * (1 - 0.30 cache) ≈ 2.49B tokens/month (steady-state)
- Estimated unit cost delivered: ~$12–$18 / 1M tokens (better unit economics due to higher tokens/sec)
- Ballpark monthly commit price: $110k–$150k/mo

Notes & recommended autoscale policy:
- Start with A100 baseline if the customer wants lower committed spend; offer H100 for critical low-latency routes.
- Recommend a hybrid policy: reserve H100s for the latency-critical route and route batch jobs to A100 pool.
- Configure autoscale to allow bursts to H100 pool for up to 30% of peak, use prefix/KV caching aggressively to lower steady-state cost.

Next steps:
- Dylan: confirm FinLytics priorities (cost vs latency) and which routes are latency-critical.
- If they choose H100 baseline, we’ll prepare a formal quote and talk about lead time for provisioning (typically 2–4 weeks for Dedicated).

I’ll put these into a short PDF and share — attaching preliminary pricing sheet.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — pricing & sizing follow-up (GPU type, reserved size, throughput)

Team —

Thanks for the detailed breakdown, Marissa — this is exactly what we needed. Quick feedback from our side:
- We prefer the H100 latency-optimized config for our live API route if we can keep unit cost under ~$20/1M tokens. Given your numbers, the H100 config looks reasonable if pricing lands at the lower half of the $110k–$150k range.
- We also like the hybrid recommendation: reserve 6x H100 for live + 8x A100 for batch. Please include a model migration path in the proposal (how we move from q4_0 to q8_0 or H100-optimized kernels), and estimated provisioning lead times.

Next steps:
1) Dylan — please send a formal proposal (config + monthly commit + SLA summary + estimated $/1M tokens) to our procurement contact, cc'ing legal.
2) We’ll review internally and schedule a final pricing call next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Tom
Tom Alvarez
CTO, FinLytics
